newsitem.title: USA: Reno,SEC,NASD queried on mob/small-cap allegations.
newsitem.headline: Reno,SEC,NASD queried on mob/small-cap allegations.

text.p: U.S. House Commerce Committee ranking member John Dingell has written to U.S. Attorney General Janet Reno and the heads of the SEC and NASD to ask what they are doing about alleged organised crime infiltration of the small-capital stock market.

Dingell, in a Feb. 6 letter to Reno, Securities and Exchange Commission Chairman Arthur Levitt and National Association of Securities Dealers Regulation President Mary Schapiro, quoted Business Week as saying "Organized crime is infiltrating the small-cap stock market, and neither the NASD nor the authorities are taking it as seriously as they should." A copy of his letter was released Monday.

Dingell, a Michigan Democrat, said: "If true, this is an outrage," and asked Reno, Levitt and Schapiro to report to him by Feb 28 "on the extent of this problem and what you have done and what you plan to do in the future to address it."

A Dec 16 article in Business Week said a three-month investigation by the magazine showed "substantial elements of the small-cap market have been turned into a veritable Mob franchise, under the very noses of regulators and law enforcement.

"... the Mob makes money in various ways, ranging from exploiting IPOs to extortion to getting a 'piece of the action' from traders and brokerage firms. But its chief means of livelihood is ripping off investors by ... driving share prices upwards and dumping them on the public through aggressive cold-calling," the magazine said.
